restrictions.text: Use a maximum of three colours including the background.
Use a maximum of two typefaces.
Do not use stock photography.
No gradients.
No drop shadows or glow effects.
The layout must work when printed in one colour.
All body copy must be at least 10pt at final print size.
Text and background must meet a 4.5:1 contrast ratio.
The headline must be readable from three metres away.
Keep the layout to a single column on mobile.
No more than seven words in the headline.
Include 3 mm bleed on every printed item.
The logo may not be enlarged beyond 20% of the canvas width.
Do not rotate or distort the logo.
Every element must sit on a defined grid.
Use only one photographic image.
No illustration or icons.
Keep the palette to greyscale plus a single accent.
All corners must be either fully square or fully rounded — do not mix.
Deliver everything as vector artwork.
The design must remain legible at 10% of its final size.
No centred text blocks.
Do not use the colour red.
Keep file size under 500 KB per digital asset.
The design must work on both a light and a dark background.
Leave a clear space equal to the logo height around every edge.
Do not use italics.
Any pattern must be built from a single repeating unit.
Include a visible call to action in the top half of the layout.
The primary message must survive being cropped to a square.

success_criteria: The main message is understood within three seconds.
The hierarchy is unambiguous: it is obvious what to read first, second and third.
The brief's stated restrictions are all respected.
Every required content item is present.
The work is legible at its real final size, not just on screen at 200%.
Colour contrast is sufficient for the audience described.
The result would be recognisable as the same brand alongside the other deliverables.
Files are supplied in the formats a real client could actually use.
The concept could be explained in one sentence.
Nothing in the composition is there only because it was easy to add.
